Messages.Body:
In article <elfholme...@netcom.com>, elfh...@netcom.com (Mark
Havener) wrote:

> In article <4e8ikc$4...@tribune.usask.ca>,
> Shane Travis <tra...@duke.usask.ca> wrote:
> >NCascone (ncas...@aol.com) wrote:

[The ongoing melodrama ;)]

> I won't try to debate the arguments above (though I might point out
that
> if several of the students in the class were having problems, it
*might*
> be more appropriate to assign extra homework to the
class...particularly
> if you only have a certain amount of time to allocate to each
student).
> The question is, which is more important to you. You, obviously, favor
> that answers be precise rather than use the minimum thought necessary.
I
> favor the latter. My group plays in a room provided by a game store,
and
> anyone is invited to stop by and play with us. It is much easier for
> "drop-ins" if we play with as few house rules as possible.

I agree about "house rules", but usually "drop-ins" are handled by a
large gaming group I go to with "no repeat actions, no vote push" and
that's that.

> <discussion of elegance coming through hard work deleted>
>
> I'm not sure which side has put more "hard work" into their fix...but
> I'll tell you this: if I started seeing a game as work, then I'd stop
> playing. "Hard work" implies that you are striving against something.
> I hardly think playing a game over and over (even if you are trying
new
> things constantly) is "hard work". Again, if you see the game as hard
> work, maybe you should find something more pleasurable to spend your
free
> time on.

I disagree. Hard work means to strive _for_ something. I _love_ to play
Jyhad, and I guess I feel the "hard work" comes from trying to make the
game even more fun to play. As for seeing a game as hard work being a
negative thing, I've been working on my own game system for almost three
years (editing/playtesting/revising/losing possible artists/etc...), and
its been lots of "hard work", but I've loved it. In regards to Jyhad, it
takes more thought to figure out a pair of "Golden Tenets" then to slap a
4CL. For other CLs, it took more thinking then a 4CL. But whatever the
"fix", thinking through the ramifications of what your change is doing to
the game is a lot more work than importing a rule from another game.

> >How does this apply to the CL/NCL debate? In this way:
> >
> >The 4CL is indeed 'simpler' than targetted solutions; as a 'first
pass'
> >it does the job acceptably with a minimum of fuss, much in the same
way
> >that breaking a table over someone's head will cause them to lose
> >consciousness - effective, but not elegant.
>
> As more and more expansions come out for V:TES, your list of house
rules
> will be forced to grow (broken cards are inevitable...they are a
problem
> with every game, not just games produced by WOTC...though they are more
> of a problem in some games than others). Eventually, I will reach the
> point where I'd *rather* have a table broken over my head than remember
a
> bunch of rules that essentially create a different game. Whatever you
> think about CL, it should be apparent that they change the rules of the
> game a lot less than inventing new rules. This will become even more
> apparent as more house rules become necessary to make a NL environment
work.

Your point about house rules is relatively unimportant, as many other
people's arguements about house rules have been. Maintaining house rules
is no more difficult than maintaining erratad rulings. If you play by
even some of the DTR's rulings, you have a set of house rules. And
secondly, one can ignore house rules just as easily as one can ignore the
DTR (example, my group and Rotschreck). In my own group, the only house
rules we use are reality check rules: things controlled by a vampire are
contested like titles, "Golden Tenets", misprints, and a little (D)
action stuff. Regardless of what else the DTR says, we don't add any
more unless we feel they make the game make more sense. Even if _I_ (or
we) feel that Werewolf Pack ought to be changed to make it a decent card,
we don't. SInce the DTR errata is the same as an "official" set of house
rules, any arguement against maintaining a set of house rules attacks
playing by the DTR.

> >The specific House Rules on broken cards are an effort to try and
apply
> >force _only where necessary_, and not as a blanket solution. While
they
> >do work (at least, some combination of them usually does the trick)
they
> >fall down where the 'simplicity' factor kicks in. There is no denying
> >that it _is_ more difficult to remember many rules than to remember
one;
> >it is also more difficult to do something well than to do it poorly,
but
> >that _in and of itself_ is not a reason for doing it poorly.

> Well/poorly, that's a matter of opinion, and I don't think it's
relevant
> here (I think the CL solution fixes V:TES' problems just as well as the
> Golden Tenets). It's also more difficult to wring stones for juice
than
> oranges, but is that a good reason to drink "stone juice" each morning
> instead of orange juice? No.

What about weenie vote push?

> >The 'Golden Tenets' are (so far) the ultimate in elegance. They look at
> >an overall _class_ of problems and fix them in a way that is, while a
> >little sloppier than targetted rules, acceptable to all. As for
> >simplicity, two rules are not significantly more difficult to remember
> >than one and they pass this test as well.

> This is not true, even by your definition. Since you haven't assigned
> "weights" to your four "factors" of elegance, a fix that is better in
one
> factor (precision) but worse in another (level of thought/work
necessary)
> is no better than the fix you are comparing it to.

> >Given, people will say that there are cards which are still broken which
> >are not fixed by these two rules. This means that the cycle will have to
> >start again - but hopefully not from scratch. Jut because a specific
> >vehicular design doesn't work, the engineers don't go back and reinvent
> >the wheel! They start from where it last _did_ work. The 'Golden Tenets'
> >are the last place where things did work; no blanket limits were necessary
> >and every card was accounted for.

> Exactly my point. Your list of rules to fix the problem will continue
to
> grow and get more and more complicated, while mine stays the same.

The only point to add to that, is if your list stays the same, your game
will grow more broken. CL doesn't stop weenie vote push, and since you
advocate not having to remember a set of added rules (a la DTR's errata,
which is _certainly_ alot of things to remember), bad unique cards
(Castle Heidelburg) hurt your playing environment.

In article <4eaqkb$4...@newsbf02.news.aol.com>, ncas...@aol.com
(NCascone) wrote:

> In article <4e8ikc$4...@tribune.usask.ca>, tra...@duke.usask.ca (Shane
> Travis) writes:

[>>CL=table over the head analogy]

> OK, CL's are a table over the head. To me, GT's that know they'll have to
> expand are like Archie Andrews' car: patched together, needing more and
> more repairs, always in danger of breaking down. Bottom line -- I don't
> want to have to suffer through a deck built with 10 Thoughts Betrayed
> because the card is busted and no one "official" has gotten around to
> making up a new GT.

Why should the Golden Tenets increase? So far, no other _class_ of
problem's has shown itself to be a problem. As for 10 Thoughts Betrayad,
what about infinite? Carlotta is wholly capable of that... Beyond
fixing classes of problems (something that both CL and GT attempt to do),
individual broken cards will always be a problem in both environments,
especially the unique cards and Carlotta'd cards.

> Breaking a table over someone's head is faster, and it lets you get on
> with what you were doing before you had to do it. I never heard of the
> GT's before I ggot online, and not many of the people I play with have net
> access. CL's work better, faster, and clearer than 2 or 3 or 5 or however
> many "Golden" tenets. This is all completely subjective, anyway 8).

I doubt many people outside of those who have access to this newsgroup,
the VTES mailing lists, and the people they play with have heard of the
GTs. Whether people have heard of them or not, this doesn't make things
any more difficult in telling a new person about them. As for working
better, no. Weenie Vote Deck counterexample (a CL deck beating up 5 NL
decks because of vote push, a GT). Faster, yes, but I have a lot of
female friends who will tell you that faster isn't always better. 1CL
and 20CL is just as fast as 10% or 6 or 4. Clearer, just barely. No
repeatable actions and no vote push takes about 10 seconds to explain.

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
ncas...@aol.com (NCascone) writes:
>First, Carlotta does not provide an infinite number of anything
>automatically. You sure put a lot of stock behind a 1-stealth action!

>The GT's _will_ increase. I base that on WotC's past performance.
>Thoughts Betrayed, Heidelberg Castle, Toreador Grand Ball, all broken.
>Maybe they'll make rulings that change the wording of the cards; however
>they deal with these obviously unplaytested cards, it'll be more rules to
>remember. CL helps by limiting the appearance of these cards in actual
>play.

Eventually, with the Lightning Bolt effect, 4CL _will_ become stricter.
Either by grouping cards into a pseudo restricted list, or my moving
to 3CL.

As more cards are introduced, changes will have to be made (unless
playtesting really does become a part of the release path) no
matter what set of rules (4CL, 2GT, etc.) you currently find
acceptable.

BTW, my "female friends" like it fast sometimes . . . but now we've gone
from bashing heads to making love . . . actually, I kind of like the
progression . . .

No, I put a lot of stock in a Carlotta deck. Dominate, Obfuscate,
Necromancy, Potence. In a Thoughts Betrayed deck, wait until you have a
TB in hand before going for more. With Obfuscate you can easily stealth
through. Necromancy to S:CE out of blocking and trying again next turn.
Carlotta could be put into a Malk deck of any type (Crazy Combat, S&B,
whatever), a Nosferatu deck, or a Giovanni centered deck, not to mention
any other deck that you care to put her in just for her special ability.
I have here in a NL deck in which the disciplines are Auspex and
Thaumaturgy (with TB thrown in for spice). Given a deck that protects
her, Carlotta is extremely tough in CL. In NL, she is just convenient.

> The GT's _will_ increase. I base that on WotC's past performance.

> Maybe they'll make rulings that change the wording of the cards; however

The GTs are not going to increase unless some class of problems present
themselves. Despite the overall botching of DS, no such class of
problems has occurred. As for individual cards needing fixing (a la
House Rules), CL/NL are in the same boat. Unless one plays without
listening to _anything_ the DTR says, a list of rules to remember will
continue to grow. Or do you play with Blythe Candeleria as printed? CL
does not hold down any list of rules.

NL

> Weenie vote is broken, but the GT is no fix by itself. I played the WV
> deck against 2 others and both opponents quit. Total votes used to push:
> 0. Voting's busted, too. What are we going to do about it?

I've never believed voting is busted. Show me a vote deck that is
degenerate under the Golden Tenets. As for both opponents quitting
without you needing to push a vote, I am surprised. Most decks should
have a reasonable amount of defense against any major strategy (vote,
bleed, combat). Not needing to push a vote means that they likely had no
vote defense, or you got an excellent draw while they drew poorly. I
repeat again, show me a vote deck that is degenerate under NL/GT.

> > Faster, yes, but I have a lot of
> >female friends who will tell you that faster isn't always better. 1CL
> >and 20CL is just as fast as 10% or 6 or 4. Clearer, just barely. No

> Good playtesting would avoid this, but in it's absence CL's help. I'm not
> sure what you mean by fast, from the above. Surely "time it takes to
> explain" is pretty low on the priority list of comparisons between NL and
> CL . . .

I was assuming your "fast" came from explaining to new people your set of
house rules. We missed each other there. :) As for being able to go out
and play "with a minimum of degeneracy", this occurs in NL as well,
because by the time we play cards such as Heidelburg Castle in a NL
environment, it usually becomes obvious that cards have potential for
disruption (as would happen in CL), but decks are not yet built with this
potential in mind.

> BTW, my "female friends" like it fast sometimes . . . but now we've gone
> from bashing heads to making love . . . actually, I kind of like the
> progression . . .

<Laughs>
Note I said "... isn't always better." When I was looking over what I
sent out, I thought I might catch heat for that last analogy, and I'm
glad it was taken in humor (at least, I _think_ it was). Maybe we should
start a new thread...
Nah, that'd be too off-topic. ;)

Messages.Body:
L. Scott Johnson (sjoh...@math.scarolina.edu) wrote:

: Eventually, with the Lightning Bolt effect, 4CL _will_ become stricter.

: Either by grouping cards into a pseudo restricted list, or my moving
: to 3CL.

: As more cards are introduced, changes will have to be made (unless
: playtesting really does become a part of the release path) no
: matter what set of rules (4CL, 2GT, etc.) you currently find
: acceptable.

: --
: L. Scott Johnson (sjoh...@math.sc.edu) | Any sufficiently advanced bug is
: http://www.math.sc.edu/~sjohnson | indistinguishable from a feature.
: Graphics Specialist and V:tES Rulemonger. | -- Kulawiec

Well, it's about time someone finally said that... And it's absolutely
true. On the one hand, people say there will never need to be additional
golden tenets because the tenets are not based on single cards, but on
idea principles. However, the no-repeat actions tenet would not have been
necessary if not for a few (what, 4? 5?) cards that allow untapping. What
may not be a problem with a single card now may become a much more
devastating one when similiar cards under the same discipline or same
cards under different disciplines are created.
The CL's will eventually have to change as well, unfortunately,
although I think that 4CL [which, as I have stated before, we play by]
will stand for some time to come. But yes, the Lightning Bolt-Chain
Lightning-Incinerate effect will occur, as long as WotC creates new
expansions. There is only so much that can be done with a given
discipline [especially in the cases of Obfuscate, Auspex and Fortitude;
Discplines like Protean lend themselves to vast variety beyond any powers
in the original V:TM].
While each may desire on playing method or the other now, as these
methods change, so might someone's opinions about which is better.

I saw a Carlotta based deck for the first time last night. 4 Carlotta's,
and The rest either IC, Justicar, or a 9 or 10 sized vamps with useful
special abilities. The library contained 4 Praxis:Solomon to stop
contestment; 6 Deals with the Devil and 2 Fragments of the Book of Nod to
get cards to the graveyard. Minion Taps and Blood Dolls to regain blood,
as well as other blood factory cards (Hunting Ground, Palatial Estate).
Most of the deck consisted of only 1 copy of a particular card (after
all, once it's in the ashheap...). The most interesting part was
Carlotta had Safe Haven on her. In a deck with good obfuscate, Thoughts

Yeah, I can think of a _lot_ of decks that would struggle under a
1CL for uniques. I know it's going to spawn a jihad (as in holy war) but
I've got to say it: what you're playing is barely recognizable as Jyhad.
Want to play a crypt of big vamps without getting hammered in the
early going? Sorry, only 1 Info Highway in your library. Want your Brujah
to intercept some actions? Well better hope the action is at only +1
stealth because it's going to be damn hard to find a KCRG News Radio to
help out your sports bike. A Ventrue voting deck gets to put in 1 Ventrue
HQ? A master-intensive strategy had better be a voting strategy as well
because you may be able to pass a Rumors of Gehenna but you'll be damn
lucky to get Anson out of your crypt.
I mean, if I squint I can see the reasoning for playing 4CL: little
worry about broken-card stategies. What is the reason for a 1CL on uniques?
Is there some glaring problem that this rule fixes that is worth crippling
dozens of deck designs for?
You know, you can't even form an all-Ravnos or all-Giovanni crypt
under these limits. Deck design is no longer a matter of what cards work
best for a strategy, but rather finding any cards that remotely relate to
the strategy.
And a 1CL on uniques adds a _lot_ more lucky to the game. If a
powerful unique is in the top 20% of your deck, you have a significant
advantage over when it's in the bottom 20%.
---



All I can really say is that we play this and it seems to work well, we
played it the without, and there seemed to be a lot more messy situations,
and a lot more contesting of cards that just made the game boring (but
quick). If you don't like it, or don't want to play it, then fine, no skin
off my nose. All I can say is that we've found that this works well in
conjunction with 4CL, it will probably affect NL badly, but NL is NL, and
putting on any restriction is betraying the concept of that style of play.
I'm not saying that NL or 4CL are better than the other, its just a matter
of personal taste and I personally prefer 4CL, as it means that you have to
think about all aspects of deck construction, rather than just a single
tactic - some say that this ruins the fun of the game, but if there are
people who enjoy playing it then surely that is okay too. As for the
comment on Ravnos and Giovanni, all I can say is that we have found that
for the majority of decks, one clan crypts just don't work.
The game we play means that there is very little room for effectiveness of
a deck design, which means that the games can be PLAYED at a more tactical
level, even for players who've constructed a deck using only 2 or 3 starter
decks of cards. This means that each game can be more challenging, even if
your deck isn't the best in the group, rather than watching one deck go
through everyone simultaneously, as no one can stop them.

Ben

Ben and I have exchanged mail on this and I think it's another
situation of "we'll have to agree to disagree." To summarize my responses
to the points above:

"I personally prefer 4CL, as it means that you have to think about all

aspects of deck construction, rather than just a single tactic" -- NL can
focus somewhat more narrowly on offensive strategies if you desire to, but
still has to defend against the broad spectrum of predator strategies
(vote, rush, S&B, weenies, etc.) I think the CL crowd exaggerates the
focusing aspects of NL.

"As for the comment on Ravnos and Giovanni, all I can say is that we have

found that for the majority of decks, one clan crypts just don't work" --
this could well be a side effect of a 1CL on uniques and 4CL overall; you
are limited to 4 Consanguineous Boons, and 1 of clan-specific uniques such
as Hunting Grounds, Spawning Pool, Storm Sewers, Art Museum, etc. I've
certainly seen effective single-clan decks in NL.

"...rather than watching one deck go through everyone simultaneously, as
no one can stop them" -- maybe my group is incompetent, but I haven't had
this "unstoppability" phenomenon. A Weenie Vote Deck is the only one I
would really worry about, and I'd rather put in one house rule to stop a
WVD, than another rule (such as low CL) that stops dozens of deck designs.
